extraction_notes: '...to complete projectsSkyline Solutions, Portland, ME, Product Manager' — the newline between the Morris and Stern bullet list and the Skyline Solutions job header is lost. Two separate employment entries are fused into one string. Section-splitting will assign the Skyline role to the wrong employer.
'• C Agile methodologies including Scrum and Kanban' — a stray 'C' from a bullet/checkbox glyph.
Home location (Miami, FL) does not match any employment location (Portland, ME). Not an error — but a detector using geographic-consistency heuristics would be misled.

spans.subject: candidate
spans.note: Skyline Solutions line — the one fused to the preceding bullet. If the deconstructor mis-sections here, this span may be attributed to the wrong field, which changes which tier evaluates it. Tests robustness of field attribution, not just detection.

spans.subject: third_party
spans.note: NOT PII, but sensitive in a way the policy table does not currently model. This is the employer the candidate is APPLYING TO, named in their own summary. It discloses active job-search intent and a specific target. If a resume were ever processed on behalf of a different employer, this leaks that the candidate is interviewing elsewhere. Flagged for the round-2 register — 'sensitive but not personal data' is a category the spec has no slot for.

spans.subject: candidate
spans.note: Two surnames joined by 'and' — the classic law/consultancy firm shape. NER will very likely return this as PERSON or as two PERSONs. If phase-1 PERSON tokenization fires here, the employer name is destroyed in the output. Highest false-positive risk in this document.

negative_controls.note: CONTRAST — as the candidate's given name in ih-001 it is a true positive. Listed here to flag that 'Ivy' does not recur elsewhere; a standalone hit would be a false positive. No standalone occurrence exists in this document.
